lesson_body:
Welcome to our first day of Unit 4: Counting Base! Today, we will embark on an exciting adventure in the world of numbers. We know that counting is one of the foundational skills in mathematics, and we will explore how we can count objects using different methods.

To kick things off, let’s gather in a circle and share how we count with our fingers! Counting on fingers is a fun way to remind us of numbers 1 through 10. I will show you how to hold up one finger for '1', two for '2', and so on. Let’s practice together by counting to five and then back again. Can everyone show me five fingers? Awesome! Now, let’s clap our hands as we count. One clap for one, two claps for two, and let’s do this all the way to five. Excellent work!

Next, we will engage in a fun story about animals in the jungle. I will read ‘Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed.’ While I read, you will see little pictures of the monkeys on the board. After the story, we will count how many monkeys are jumping together on each page. This activity helps us learn to recognize numbers and understand that numbers can represent the quantity of objects around us. We will pay special attention to how we say each number and use our voices to represent the numbers loud and clear!

To end our lesson, let’s practice counting with some colorful counting bears. I will give each of you a small handful of these bears, and we will work together to count how many bears we each have. Remember to count them one by one. Afterward, we will arrange our bears into groups of four. This will help us understand both counting and the concept of grouping numbers! Remember, counting is not just about saying the numbers, but it’s about understanding how many we have of something. 

As we finish our day, let’s gather back in our circle and recap what we’ve learned. Counting is fun, and it’s an essential skill that will help us in math as we grow. Great job today, everyone! Let's keep practicing our counting at home too!
interactive_assignment:
For today’s hands-on activity, we will create our very own Counting Collage! First, gather in small groups with your classmates and collect different items from around the classroom—these could be buttons, paper clips, crayons, or scraps of colored paper. Each group will receive a large piece of construction paper. 

Next, you will work together to count how many items you have collected and write the number at the top of your construction paper. Then, you will glue the items onto your collage. For example, if you have four buttons, you will glue them on and write '4' where they are placed.  Each group will share their collage with the class, explaining how they counted their items and what number they represented. This creative assignment will not only reinforce your counting skills but also allow you to work collaboratively with your friends!

daily_assessment.question: How many fingers do you hold up when you count to 3?
